chunk.text: If we put it simply, objectively, we can agree that the rest of the teams may or may not belong there, but one team nobody can question is Arsenal. They are number one in the Premier League, they are number one in the Champions League, they are number one in the FA Cup semi-final as well, if I am not mistaken. They are number one in the Carabao Cup semi-final as well, if I am not mistaken. And if we look at the table, I had seen that in the Premier League, they are the third team with the most time lost to injuries, meaning players were out injured for a long time. So Chonky said that you plan for the Champions League, all those things.

Now see, they are third, with 603 days lost to injuries, this is for this season. Newcastle is number one here, and they are also number one in the Champions League in the top 8. Is it too much about planning? Who do you give credit to? This whole project of Arsenal is dangerous. If someone points out a single key reason that has made them the most different in Europe, that's why they are number one. I think the reason for this is pretty common, and everyone will have the same answer, it's Arteta. It's simply the time that this project has taken. It's not like the squad was built overnight. Their defensive depth has been built, the options in midfield, and let's just say they had attackers like Gabriel Jesus, Victor Osimhen,

but despite their absence, they play Mikel Merino sometimes. The variety of players they have brought allows them to play in multiple positions. Declan Rice, Zubimendi, being backups, can also play together at the same time. Technically, if Mikel Merino is not there, Declan Rice operates in the number 8 position, but if Zubimendi is not there, he will drop deeper. So I would say this project is built over time. If someone points it out, we all here would give the credit to Mikel Arteta for this. But I will say one thing from the bottom of my heart, that trophies are a different subject, but what Arsenal is doing right now this season, I think this is what Mikel Arteta has earned. People say there are so many coaches who have actually won trophies,

I myself say this, that you should not compare Mikel Arteta with them because they have won trophies and Mikel Arteta has not. But then I ask, how many managers do you see who have successfully built a side like this, sitting at the top of their league, sitting at the top in the Champions League, undefeated? I mean, they have won all their matches, and they didn’t even have easy fixtures. They played Inter and completely dominated them, they defeated Bayern this season convincingly, Atletico Madrid too, they beat them 4-1, and these are not small teams. Atletico Madrid, completely outclassed in the semi-finals.

Muktesh, you raised an interesting point regarding Arsenal, which is their first goal against Inter. If you had seen it, it was like Timber, what a cross from Timber to Gabriel Jesus, it was crazy football. Then you see, their football in the Premier League is a little different, it feels a little slower. I think Arteta had said that in the Premier League, teams prefer not to play with the ball, they feel comfortable without possession. Inter did not do that, Inter attacked a bit, but their counter-attack was a little slow. But as Chonky pointed out, the first goal defines Arteta’s football. I am not sure if it was the first goal from a corner, no, it was the second goal. The first goal was a back-heel involving Timber and space.

And it was one of the best goals scored during this game week. Arsenal’s biggest strength is that they are very good in tight spaces, which used to be the strength of Man City at one time. Man City used to operate like this, now Arsenal is doing that. The point of difference was that he put Gyokeres on the bench and brought Jesus, and that complemented the players on the pitch against Inter Milan. And I think Arteta, again, Muktesh has said a lot of things, but squad depth is crazy. I heard that they can make two teams, one with only left-footed players and one with only right-footed players, both being good teams. The recruitment they have done is not just about scoring goals, they have also solved depth through recruitment.

So that in case injury issues arise, which unfortunately they have faced, and they are competing on all fronts, their options and alternatives can cover for them. Also, the flexibility they have shown in recruitment ensures that players not only cover their own position but also other positions. Today, Bukayo Saka has an alternative in Madueke. If Gyokeres is unavailable, Gabriel Jesus can step in. Declan Rice can cover for Jurrien Timber, Zubimendi can play multiple roles, Merino can move forward, Madueke can play anywhere. Versatility is key. If we talk about the squad and injuries, I will take a small point, I don’t want to know your opinion.

It often happens that managers are rightly blamed. A manager’s primary job is to keep the team fit. If you are playing football, the coach ensures you are fit first. Managers do get blamed for fitness concerns, along with their fitness team. Some managers have more injuries in their squads. I don’t know why, especially considering the money spent over the years, particularly in defense. Their entire defense has been chronically injured. I don’t see many people talking about Arteta’s methods in terms of fitness preparation. This is a unique problem. They buy a new center-back every year, often versatile players, because their players keep getting injured repeatedly.

I think this is completely reasonable if you look at their defensive record over the last three seasons. In terms of chances conceded, goals conceded, and xG conceded, they have been among the best across Europe, not just in the Premier League. This level cannot be achieved without demanding a lot from your defenders. So it feels reasonable that their defenders are the most heavily used players on the pitch. We also know how much work they contribute even in the opponent’s box. If you look at their set-piece routines, they involve a lot of physicality from defenders.

But if you look at Gabriel Jesus’ goal from a corner, that delivery was more about distracting markers who were focused on their tall defenders. Gabriel Jesus is not a tall player, so in a crowded central area, you wouldn’t expect him to latch onto such a cross. But opponents were busy marking the physically dominant defenders. This aligns with their defensive recruitment philosophy, which is based on their core idea of being defensively solid first. Arteta is praised, but the reality is this project needs to win. That major trophy is long overdue. If it wins now, then it makes sense. Otherwise, the question remains, if not now, then when?

They have been absolutely poor, they don’t deserve it. And I am a little frustrated with Arsenal because technically, if you look at Aston Villa and Manchester City, both teams have dropped points in three matches each. If they had not dropped points, they would be ahead of Arsenal right now. Manchester City would be two points ahead, and Aston Villa would be one point ahead. So this complacency is concerning. Even though we know Arsenal has the quality to win, from a team that has performed so well in Europe, it is disappointing.

I wanted them to keep increasing their lead. Even if it was just 1%, I would be personally disappointed about why they let this happen. Isn’t that the beauty of league football? For example, if others hadn’t dropped points, they would be ahead, so why are Arsenal dropping points? And if teams are catching up despite dropping points, it means they are improving too. If you look at Aston Villa, compared to two years ago, they are playing so well. Newcastle is doing well, Bournemouth is also decent. But your point is clear, despite all this, the table shows that they are the third most injured team.
Still, they are top of every competition.
